en: Ecclesiastes 1

p.src: 1  The words of the Preacher, the son of David, king in Jerusalem:

en: The words of the Preacher, the son of David, king in Jerusalem:
u.src: 1  The words of the Preacher, the son of David, king in Jerusalem:

p.src: 2  “Vanity of vanities,” says the Preacher; “Vanity of vanities, all is vanity.”

en: “Vanity of vanities,” says the Preacher; “Vanity of vanities, all is vanity.”
u.src: 2  “Vanity of vanities,” says the Preacher; “Vanity of vanities, all is vanity.”

p.src: 3  What does man gain from all his labor in which he labors under the sun?

en: What does man gain from all his labor in which he labors under the sun?
u.src: 3  What does man gain from all his labor in which he labors under the sun?

p.src: 4  One generation goes, and another generation comes; but the earth remains forever.

en: One generation goes, and another generation comes; but the earth remains forever.
u.src: 4  One generation goes, and another generation comes; but the earth remains forever.

p.src: 5  The sun also rises, and the sun goes down, and hurries to its place where it rises.

en: The sun also rises, and the sun goes down, and hurries to its place where it rises.
u.src: 5  The sun also rises, and the sun goes down, and hurries to its place where it rises.

p.src: 6  The wind goes toward the south, and turns around to the north. It turns around continually as it goes, and the wind returns again to its courses.

en: The wind goes toward the south, and turns around to the north. It turns around continually as it goes, and the wind returns again to its courses.
u.src: 6  The wind goes toward the south, and turns around to the north. It turns around continually as it goes, and the wind returns again to its courses.

p.src: 7  All the rivers run into the sea, yet the sea is not full. To the place where the rivers flow, there they flow again.

en: All the rivers run into the sea, yet the sea is not full. To the place where the rivers flow, there they flow again.
u.src: 7  All the rivers run into the sea, yet the sea is not full. To the place where the rivers flow, there they flow again.

p.src: 8  All things are full of weariness beyond uttering. The eye is not satisfied with seeing, nor the ear filled with hearing.

en: All things are full of weariness beyond uttering. The eye is not satisfied with seeing, nor the ear filled with hearing.
u.src: 8  All things are full of weariness beyond uttering. The eye is not satisfied with seeing, nor the ear filled with hearing.

p.src: 9  That which has been is that which shall be, and that which has been done is that which shall be done; and there is no new thing under the sun.

en: That which has been is that which shall be, and that which has been done is that which shall be done; and there is no new thing under the sun.
u.src: 9  That which has been is that which shall be, and that which has been done is that which shall be done; and there is no new thing under the sun.

p.src: 10  Is there a thing of which it may be said, “Behold, this is new”? It has been long ago, in the ages which were before us.

en: Is there a thing of which it may be said, “Behold, this is new”? It has been long ago, in the ages which were before us.
u.src: 10  Is there a thing of which it may be said, “Behold, this is new”? It has been long ago, in the ages which were before us.

en: 1:10 “Behold”, from “הִנֵּה”, means look at, take notice, observe, see, or gaze at. It is often used as an interjection.

p.src: 11  There is no memory of the former; neither shall there be any memory of the latter that are to come, among those that shall come after.

en: There is no memory of the former; neither shall there be any memory of the latter that are to come, among those that shall come after.
u.src: 11  There is no memory of the former; neither shall there be any memory of the latter that are to come, among those that shall come after.

p.src: 12  I, the Preacher, was king over Israel in Jerusalem.

en: I, the Preacher, was king over Israel in Jerusalem.
u.src: 12  I, the Preacher, was king over Israel in Jerusalem.

p.src: 13  I applied my heart to seek and to search out by wisdom concerning all that is done under the sky. It is a heavy burden that God has given to the sons of men to be afflicted with.

en: I applied my heart to seek and to search out by wisdom concerning all that is done under the sky. It is a heavy burden that God has given to the sons of men to be afflicted with.
u.src: 13  I applied my heart to seek and to search out by wisdom concerning all that is done under the sky. It is a heavy burden that God has given to the sons of men to be afflicted with.

en: 1:13 The Hebrew word rendered “God” is “אֱלֹהִ֑ים” (Elohim).

p.src: 14  I have seen all the works that are done under the sun; and behold, all is vanity and a chasing after wind.

en: I have seen all the works that are done under the sun; and behold, all is vanity and a chasing after wind.
u.src: 14  I have seen all the works that are done under the sun; and behold, all is vanity and a chasing after wind.

p.src: 15  That which is crooked can’t be made straight; and that which is lacking can’t be counted.

en: That which is crooked can’t be made straight; and that which is lacking can’t be counted.
u.src: 15  That which is crooked can’t be made straight; and that which is lacking can’t be counted.

p.src: 16  I said to myself, “Behold, I have obtained for myself great wisdom above all who were before me in Jerusalem. Yes, my heart has had great experience of wisdom and knowledge.”

en: I said to myself, “Behold, I have obtained for myself great wisdom above all who were before me in Jerusalem. Yes, my heart has had great experience of wisdom and knowledge.”
u.src: 16  I said to myself, “Behold, I have obtained for myself great wisdom above all who were before me in Jerusalem. Yes, my heart has had great experience of wisdom and knowledge.”

p.src: 17  I applied my heart to know wisdom, and to know madness and folly. I perceived that this also was a chasing after wind.

en: I applied my heart to know wisdom, and to know madness and folly. I perceived that this also was a chasing after wind.
u.src: 17  I applied my heart to know wisdom, and to know madness and folly. I perceived that this also was a chasing after wind.

p.src: 18  For in much wisdom is much grief; and he who increases knowledge increases sorrow.

en: For in much wisdom is much grief; and he who increases knowledge increases sorrow.
u.src: 18  For in much wisdom is much grief; and he who increases knowledge increases sorrow.
